plans.note: Section 15 is headed 'Limitation of Garman's Liability' — one-sided by title, so check cap amount, mutuality and carve-outs (IP indemnity in sec-13, confidentiality in sec-14, wilful misconduct). Confirm no double-flagging with INDEMN.

Section 13 is an express IP indemnity from Garman. Verify scope (defence plus costs, no unreasonable conduct conditions), whether it is capped by sec-15, and whether any reciprocal customer indemnity is broader than narrow.

No non-compete heading; a software licence of this type rarely restricts our business lines. Scan sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) and sec-20 general matters for any competing-product or no-build language before marking missing.
No exclusivity heading. Check the licence grant (sec-2), use restrictions (sec-3) and maintenance/fees (sec-10, sec-11) for sole-source or exclusive-supplier wording for support services.

No pricing-parity heading evident. Review fees (sec-11) and maintenance charges (sec-10) for any obligation on us to extend best terms to Garman; MFN running in our favour would be beneficial and not flagged.

Section 19 'Non-Solicitation of Employees' is squarely on point. Check mutuality, duration (12 months preferred), scope limited to employees engaged on the project, and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Section 17 (Term and Termination) is the primary locus; sections 7 and 8 give an option to reject the software pre-acceptance. Assess whether we may terminate maintenance on notice without penalty and whether Garman has a matching convenience right mid-term.

Maintenance term and renewal mechanics likely sit in sec-10 and sec-17, with uplift mechanics in sec-11. Check auto-renewal length, non-renewal notice window (30-60 days preferred) and any price-increase cap (uplift cap absence is a rationale note only).

Governing law, venue and dispute resolution will be in sec-20 General Matters. Given the Canadian/UK parties, check for a non-listed law (e.g., Nova Scotia, Ontario) or mandatory foreign arbitration versus the accepted NY/DE/CA/E&W courts.

Assignment clause expected in sec-20; licence transfer restrictions may also appear in sec-3. Confirm we may assign to affiliates and to a successor in a change of control without consent, and that Garman has no termination right on our change of control (cross-check sec-17).

Ownership statements likely in the grant (sec-2) and escrow (sec-16); our data and modifications may be addressed in sec-4 conversion work and sec-14 confidentiality. Ensure no assignment to Garman of our data, configurations or feedback.

Section 2 is the grant; sec-3 restricts use and sec-1 defines Authorized Locations/Schedules. Check that the licence is perpetual/irrevocable on payment, covers affiliates and contractors operating for our benefit, and that location or CPU limits are workable.

No audit heading; verification rights, if any, will be embedded in sec-3 use restrictions or sec-20. If present, test notice, frequency, business-hours limitation, confidentiality and Vendor-borne cost.

Look in fees (sec-11) for interest on late payment, early-termination charges or accelerated fees, and in sec-17 for termination penalties. Interest at a commercial rate is not liquidated damages; service credits in our favour are welcome.

Section 12 (Specifications and Warranty) is primary, supported by acceptance testing (sec-6) and maintenance (sec-10). Check warranty duration from acceptance, conformity-to-specification standard, remedy (repair/replace then refund), and any disclaimer in sec-12 or sec-15.

No insurance heading in the outline; check sec-20 general matters and the on-site implementation provisions (sec-4, sec-9) since Garman personnel attend our locations. Likely a missing-clause finding.
Check fees (sec-11) and maintenance (sec-10) plus the Schedules referenced in sec-1 for minimum seat/location counts, committed maintenance years or take-or-pay language with no exit.

Section 17 termination consequences and sec-18 survival are the likely homes; sec-16 escrow partially mitigates continuity but is not transition assistance or data return. Check sec-4 (data conversion) for any return-of-data mechanic before concluding it is missing.
